title: Benchmark fingerprint index and anomaly triage workflow
creator: Leena Patel
description:
Problem: Our benchmark backfill and continuous load tests produce high-dimensional time series (tokens/sec, p95 latency, error-rate, instance-level metrics). Teams spend too much time chasing noisy blips and re-running full suites to reproduce regressions. We need a compact, queryable representation (a 'fingerprint') of each run plus a lightweight comparison UI and triage workflow so engineers can quickly decide if a deviation is actionable or noise.

Goal: Build a fingerprint index service that stores compact signatures for every benchmark run (summary stats + structural signal), enable fast pairwise and cohort comparisons, add an anomaly scoring pipeline that incorporates infra/context tags, and ship a small UI flow for triage (investigate, snooze, escalate, link PRs). This ticket scopes the index design, storage schema, comparison API, triage UX props, and an initial playbook for on-call and bench owners.
acceptance_criteria: A compact JSON Line fingerprint schema is documented and reviewed (<= 20 fields, includes sample_size, p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens_per_sec, distribution_hash, infra_tags, commit_sha, run_id, started_at)
Index service ingesting daily benchmark runs: ingest latency <= 5s per run and storage per fingerprint < 2KB
Comparison API: pairwise diff returns top-5 contributing dimensions with normalized effect sizes and a simple anomaly score
Triage UI: show run timeline, top contributing deltas, infra tag filters, ability to attach GitHub PR and create a triage ticket (linear link), and a "snooze" action for transient signals
Anomaly scoring pipeline incorporates context weighting (e.g., model change, quantization, instance_type) and flags high-confidence regressions for on-call
Playbook drafted and reviewed by reliability and serving runtime teams with at least 3 run-through examples
End-to-end demo with a seeded regression: from ingestion -> alert -> triage ui -> created follow-up ticket
steps: Design fingerprint schema and storage model (kv-store vs timeseries DB)
Prototype fingerprint extractor in benchmark harness (python) and add to nightly jobs
Build index writer service with a small REST API and retention policy
Implement pairwise comparator logic and anomaly scoring heuristics
Add lightweight triage UI mockups and validate with PM/Design
Integrate UI actions with Linear and GitHub (create issue / attach PR)
Run a 2-week dogfood campaign and collect feedback
comments: 2025-02-14 | Leena Patel: Initial writeup — sketched schema and rationale. Want to keep per-run payload minimal so we can store millions of runs. Proposed fields attached in Confluence: https://confluence.internal/redwood/bench-fingerprint

2025-02-18 | Ravi Kapoor: Did a spike comparing storage backends — RocksDB local index + S3 blobs looks promising for cost. Will prototype writer using local RocksDB and a compact protobuf for fingerprints.
2025-02-22 | Priya Menon (reliability): Suggested adding kernel_version and driver_version to infra_tags — those have caused noisy regressions before.
2025-02-25 | Design review (Amir Chen): Shared low-fi triage UI; focuses on three panes: run details, top-deltas, and action panel. PM asked for 'snooze' states and confidence badges.

2025-02-27 | Ravi Kapoor: Implemented fingerprint extractor in the new harness branch (github.com/redwood/bench-harness PR #412). Extractor emits distribution_hash (hash of bucketed latency histogram) and token_rate median/iqr.

2025-03-01 | Leena Patel: Ran dogfood ingest on last 30 days of runs (sample set). Index size ~1.1GB for ~75k fingerprints (~1.5KB each). Pairwise comparator prototype flagged three regressions; two were infra-related (driver bump) — matched expectations.
2025-03-02 | Ravi Kapoor: Next: wire comparator to alerting pipeline and add triage UI endpoints (POST /triage/{run}/action). Need PM signoff on playbook examples by 2025-03-07.
